subject: Converting a list of lists to a data.frame

messages.author: f3405cd5652aa11d
messages.subject: Converting a list of lists to a data.frame
parts:
I would like to convert a list of lists to a data frame but I so far
have been unsuccessful. My latest attempt looks like:

> library(plyr)
> d <- rep(1:53,2)
> s <- ts(d, frequency=53, start=c(2000,10))
> l <- list()
> l[["test"]] <- list(name="list with ts", series=s)
> ld <- ldply(l, quickdf)

This yields the error:

Error: length(rows) == 1 is not TRUE

Any ideas?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Converting a list of lists to a data.frame
parts:
I got 106 rows, the length of the series; how many did you get? Were
you expecting 53 x 2? If you recall, the series object in your list
had a length of 106.

I'm wondering if you were expecting that the frequency, times, etc.
would be carried along for the ride; if so, the answer is no, unless
you write a function that extracts such information from the
Time-Series object such that it can be shipped to a data frame as a
return value. (I don't know whether or not it can, but str() of your
ts object wasn't encouraging.) This is why you were encouraged in
another post on R-help to think about using the zoo, xts and/or
quantmod packages. They are better equipped to handle and manipulate
time series data in various ways. Among people who analyze time series
data in R on a regular basis, very few of them use the ts class; most
of what I've seen on R-help or in time series lecture notes are the
zoo, xts and quantmod packages or the finMetrics library. All of these
are well documented; since xts and quantmod depend on zoo, it's better
to start by learning the zoo package. It has five vignettes and a demo
to get you started. xts has a vignette and quantmod has a demo; both
are geared toward financial time series, though. A book can be
downloaded from the finMetrics web site if you prefer to go that route
(it's long, though :)

Dennis
